chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-'Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of them (the Imams), upon them be peace, who said:

"When a man marries off his son's daughter, it is valid for the son, and the son may also marry her off." I said, "What if her father desires a man and her grandfather desires a man?" He said, "The grandfather is more entitled to her marriage."
ai.seo_question: Who has the right to arrange the marriage of a granddaughter if the father and grandfather disagree?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the hierarchy of marriage guardianship (wilayah al-nikah), establishing that the paternal grandfather holds precedence over the father when both are present and potentially conflicting in their choices. This ruling is central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the capacity of minors and the specific order of male agnates (aqrab) in contracting marriage for females who lack full independent agency in the matter.
